answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places that color's Player ID upright in its stand visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set with that color on the backs; remove cards targeting colors not in play and keep the player's own Ambush. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, with values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘puts its Player ID card upright in its plastic stand’; remove cards targeting colors not playing; ‘Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.’

answers.answer: There is no individual turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘There is no individual turn order.’ Vote: ‘You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed’ and ‘reveal all choices simultaneously.’

answers.answer: No. Red is the sole Target because Red's three votes are more than either other player's two. A player receiving the most votes is the Target; a majority or any fixed minimum is not stated as necessary.
answers.evidence: Vote: ‘The player receiving the most votes is the Target.’ The larger example says, ‘Blue alone is the Target: four and three are different totals.’

answers.answer: Both Red and Blue are Targets because all players tied for the most votes are Targets. With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive that requirement, subject to any other applicable elimination rule.
answers.evidence: Vote: ‘If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets’; with tied Targets, voting for any one of them ‘satisfies the voting requirement.’

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
answers.evidence: Vote: ‘Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated.’

answers.answer: Red's Ambush adds no vote. Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count, so Red and Yellow tie at one vote apiece and both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds because Red is a Target; Red can eliminate one player who voted for Red, namely Yellow. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives, and Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink remain.
answers.evidence: Three-player example: Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, Pink votes for Yellow; Red and Yellow tie, Yellow is eliminated, and Pink survives after voting for tied Target Yellow, leaving Red and Pink.

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush eliminates only one player, chosen from among the players who voted for the ambusher. They may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: chooses ‘one of the players who voted for them’; ‘They cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.’

answers.answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
answers.evidence: Ambush: ‘An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.’

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another conspiracy and vote among those surviving players; only survivors participate in the subsequent vote.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.’

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points: each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points, and the values vary.
answers.evidence: One survivor ‘collects all four central Gold Bars’; Components: ‘Gold Bars are cards, not points’ and each card's value is 3, 4, or 5 points.

answers.answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go. They may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card and places it face down. When both are ready, reveal both choices simultaneously and resolve their pairing.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: each takes ‘Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go’; they may discuss, choose one face down, and ‘reveal both choices simultaneously.’

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote do not receive this no-survivor consolation bar, including those eliminated in it. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave them for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: No survivors: ‘Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.’

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share / Share: ‘You get 2; opponent gets 2.’

answers.answer: The finalist choosing Share gets zero central bars, and the finalist choosing Steal gets all four central bars.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share / Steal: Share player gets 0 and opponent gets 4.

answers.answer: The finalist choosing Grab One & Go gets one central bar; the finalist choosing Steal gets the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go / Steal: ‘You get 1; opponent gets 3’; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: The finalist choosing Grab One & Go gets one central bar; the finalist choosing Share gets the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go / Share: ‘You get 1; opponent gets 3’; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar, and the other two remain in the center. If play continues, add two new bars to bring the central pool back to four.
answers.evidence: Both Grab One & Go: each receives one, ‘leave the other 2 in the center’; ‘add just two new bars for the next round.’

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Both Steal: ‘neither finalist receives gold’; give ‘every other player one Gold Bar from the deck’; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.

answers.answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring: check ‘at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded’; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; ‘the highest point total wins.’

answers.answer: For exactly two tied leaders at game end, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown; repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player has the highest gold point total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including all players eliminated during that round; stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied players ‘conduct another Final Showdown’ and ‘Repeat these Showdowns as necessary’; after no winner, ‘everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright.’

answers.answer: Before every vote, players discuss or signal intended targets for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, openly or secretly, including texting and showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
answers.evidence: Conspire: ‘roughly a minute and a half at most’; any method, openly or secretly, including ‘texting’ and ‘showing a Voting card’; the game owner asks for final decisions.

answers.answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the color of the player's visible ID whom you target, and place it face down in front of yourself. If you suspect you are the Target, play your own Ambush card instead.
answers.evidence: Vote: target someone with the card matching that player's visible ID color; each player places one card ‘face down in front of themselves’; play your Ambush to defend yourself.

answers.answer: Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; those survivors are eligible for the next vote in the round.
answers.evidence: Vote: ‘Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.’

answers.answer: After checking for a winner, if there is no winner everyone returns and the central pool is refilled to four cards as needed. Since all four central bars were awarded, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down, keeping their values hidden.
answers.evidence: After round rewards, if no winner everyone returns; ‘If the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars.’

answers.answer: No. Blue alone is the Target because four votes exceed Purple's three; Blue's successful Ambush does not make Purple a Target. Voters for Purple do not survive on that basis: they did not vote for the sole Target, Blue, so they are eliminated.
answers.evidence: Larger example: ‘Blue alone is the Target: four and three are different totals’; Purple does not become a Target; players who voted for Purple are eliminated for failing to vote for Blue.

answers.answer: The booklet's instruction is that tied qualifying leaders conduct a Final Showdown, repeated as necessary until one player has the highest total. It does not specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among three or more tied players; the summary marks this as unresolved and says publisher clarification is required.
answers.evidence: Scoring says tied leaders ‘conduct another Final Showdown’; the unresolved source limitation says the procedure and payoff table cover only two players and provide no arrangement for three or more.

answers.answer: Yes. The one-bar deck reward for everyone outside a double-Steal pair can make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner after comparing all players' totals.
answers.evidence: Scoring: ‘The one-bar deck reward for everyone outside a double-Steal pair can therefore make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.’
